description: Routing eval for the home-lab operations overlap: homelab-platform (the agent that owns change authority) against the eight lab skills that share its vocabulary — service-onboard, lab-audit, runbook, postmortem, lab-incident, restore-drill, upgrade-campaign, observability. They all speak of 'my lab', 'a service', 'check', 'docs', 'what happened', over a LIVE lab, so a misroute here is the most consequential in the fleet (a read-only question landing on a mutating path, or mitigation machinery firing on a finished incident). Positives name the specific intended member; negatives share the vocabulary but must route to NO cluster member.
notes: Grading (scripts/eval_routing.py): a positive passes if any member in expect_fires fired; a negative passes only if NO member fired. History: seeded with four members; postmortem joined 2026-07-24 (backlog 1.4) and lab-incident, restore-drill, upgrade-campaign and observability the same day (backlog 1.2/1.5 plus the modernization plan's remainder), so the captured baselines under baselines/2026-07/ and baselines/2026-07-24/ both predate the current 9-member case set and a full re-baseline is pending. Seams this cluster guards: (1) lab-incident vs postmortem — 'X is down' is live and mitigates, 'it's fixed, write it up' must NOT reach lab-incident (neg-resolved-not-incident). (2) service-onboard sets disable-model-invocation but ships as a plugin skill, so per anthropics/claude-code#22345 it may fire directly on 'add a service' prompts even though the intended owner is homelab-platform; that is the open routing residual, not a clean pass. (3) lab-shaping ARCHITECTURE (storage/network layout) routes UP the ladder per homelab-platform's Boundaries, not to this cluster (neg-lab-architecture).

cases.prompt: Add Jellyfin to my home lab — set up the container behind the reverse proxy with TLS.
cases.expected_output: Routes to homelab-platform, which owns change authority and works the service-onboard checklist by path. Watch: service-onboard firing as a direct Skill call (per #22345) instead of homelab-platform is the open routing residual, not the intended path.

cases.prompt: My Pi-hole container was set up ad-hoc — no health check, no backups, no runbook. Bring it up to standard.
cases.expected_output: The 'bring an existing ad-hoc service up to standard' path — homelab-platform working the service-onboard checklist under its tiers.

cases.prompt: My reverse proxy keeps returning 502 for the Grafana route. Figure out why and fix it.
cases.expected_output: Troubleshooting live infrastructure — homelab-platform, under its change tiers (the fix is a Tier 2 apply).

cases.prompt: Pin the Jellyfin image off :latest to a specific version and restart the stack.
cases.expected_output: A deliberate versioned change to a running stack — homelab-platform's worked Tier 2 example is literally this.

cases.prompt: What's wrong with my home lab? Do a health and hygiene sweep and tell me what needs attention.
cases.expected_output: A read-only survey — lab-audit, which reports severity-ranked findings and hands fixes to homelab-platform.

cases.prompt: Audit my lab — is anything exposed to the internet, are any certs about to expire, any containers still on :latest?
cases.expected_output: Exposure/certificate/version checks are lab-audit's Checks list; read-only.

cases.prompt: Write a runbook for my Postgres container: how to check it's healthy, restart it, and recover it from backup.
cases.expected_output: An operating doc to the fixed runbook template — the runbook skill.

cases.prompt: Update the operating doc for Nextcloud with the new restart-and-verify procedure.
cases.expected_output: Updating an operating doc — runbook.

cases.prompt: Last night the whole lab lost DNS for two hours — it's fixed now. Write up what happened so we learn from it.
cases.expected_output: Resolved incident, learning-focused write-up — the postmortem skill. 'It's fixed now' is the after-recovery cue that separates this from live-failure routing.

cases.prompt: Do a postmortem on yesterday's Nextcloud outage — the disk filled up and it was down all afternoon.
cases.expected_output: Named explicitly; cause already known (disk full), so no root-cause loop needed — straight to the blameless write-up.

cases.prompt: Add a CSV export feature to my web app's reports page.
cases.expected_output: Application code — routes to a builder (sde-fullstack / frontend-craft), not lab ops. 'Add' is shared vocabulary with add-a-service.

cases.prompt: Review my deploy script's pull request for security bugs before I merge it.
cases.expected_output: Reviewing a diff — code-reviewer. 'Deploy' and 'review' share vocabulary with lab work but this is a code review.

cases.prompt: My integration test for the API fails about one run in five. Find out why.
cases.expected_output: Debugging a flaky test — root-cause. 'Find out why' shares vocabulary with troubleshooting, but there is no lab here.

cases.prompt: Write API documentation for the public functions in my Python library.
cases.expected_output: Library API docs are not an ops runbook — must NOT fire runbook. 'Write documentation' is the tight near-miss for runbook.

cases.prompt: I'm planning the next two years of my lab — should I run Ceph or ZFS for storage, and how should I segment the VLANs?
cases.expected_output: Lab-shaping architecture on a multi-year horizon — routes UP the ladder (distinguished/principal) per homelab-platform's Boundaries, not to the ops cluster. Guards the eng-ladder-vs-homelab seam. 'Lab' and 'storage' are shared vocabulary.

cases.prompt: Build a status-page dashboard that reads services.json and shows each service's health.
cases.expected_output: A UI build — frontend-craft / sde-fullstack. 'Services' and 'health' share vocabulary with lab monitoring, but this is app code.

cases.prompt: My Claude Code skill for lab tasks never triggers when I ask it. Fix its description.
cases.expected_output: Prompt tooling — prompt-craft / prompt-engineer. The word 'lab' is a decoy; the task is fixing a description.

cases.prompt: Write up what happened in yesterday's sprint retro and turn it into a list of action items.
cases.expected_output: Meeting notes, not an incident — must NOT fire postmortem despite sharing 'write up what happened', 'retro', and 'action items'. The tight near-miss for the new member.

cases.prompt: Everything in my lab just stopped — none of the services load and I can't reach the dashboard. Help.
cases.expected_output: An active outage, mitigate-first — lab-incident, applying under homelab-platform's tiers.

cases.prompt: Nextcloud is throwing 502s since the update an hour ago and my family can't upload anything. Get it working.
cases.expected_output: Live user-affecting failure with a known recent change — mitigate (roll back) before diagnosing.

cases.prompt: I want to actually test that my Postgres backups can be restored, before I need them. Walk me through a rehearsal.
cases.expected_output: A rehearsal into a scratch target with a measured duration — restore-drill.

cases.prompt: It's patch day — I want to update all the containers in my lab. Plan it so I don't break everything at once.
cases.expected_output: A batch of version upgrades needing ordering and per-service rollback — upgrade-campaign.

cases.prompt: Write me a Prometheus alert that tells me when my nightly backup job hasn't succeeded, and a PromQL query for the p99 latency of my reverse proxy.
cases.expected_output: Alert-rule and PromQL design — the observability skill.

cases.prompt: The DNS outage from last night is fully resolved now. Write up what happened so we learn from it.
cases.expected_output: Already resolved — this is postmortem's job, NOT lab-incident's. Guards the seam in the direction that matters: mitigation machinery must not fire on a finished incident. (postmortem firing here is correct and is covered by pos-postmortem-writeup.)

cases.prompt: Harden SSH on my lab's Ubuntu box — key-only logins, no root login, and make sure I can't lock myself out in the process.
cases.expected_output: Host-level Linux work on a lab machine — the Home-Lab SRE's substrate (the users/SSH/access-recovery vocabulary lands in the description with ROLE-001). Seeded before the rebrand: the before-anchor measures the old description, so this case's before/after diff is the direct measure of the Linux-host trigger widening.

cases.prompt: I just set up a new mini PC with a fresh Debian install for the lab. Bring it up to standard as a lab host — users and SSH, firewall, updates, monitoring, and backups.
cases.expected_output: A new machine entering the lab — homelab-platform working the host-onboard checklist. The skill joins the cluster's members when it lands (ROLE-001 edit wave); until then the agent is the only routable owner, mirroring the pos-add-service / service-onboard pattern.

cases.prompt: Partition my personal laptop and install Arch on it, then set up my dotfiles and dev tools.
cases.expected_output: A personal workstation, not the lab — no cluster member owns it. Partition/install/users/dotfiles is the decoy vocabulary for ROLE-001's Linux-host trigger widening; this is the tight near-miss that guards it.
